DS 340W Midterm Code Update

DS 340W: Fall 2026 Maeric Barrows & Ayla Orona

This is documentation for processes performed for the midterm code update.

0. Setup

Load Libraries

# Clear environment
remove(list=ls())

# General
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(rsample) # Data split
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
library(pROC) # ROC curves

# Data Pre-processing
library(smotefamily)
#library(FSelector)  # for Gain Ratio but not working so computed it manually instead
library(themis)
library(randomForest)

Load Data

Our data comes from Kaggle. It is a 20,000 observation, 16 feature dataset featuring data on patients with and without lung cancer and their symptoms.

Link: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/akashnath29/lung-cancer-dataset

# Load the dataset
lung_cancer <- read.csv("parentpaper1_data.csv")

head(lung_cancer)

1. Data Cleaning and EDA

Data Cleaning

# Convert binary variables (1, 2) to 0/1 (0=No, 1=Yes)
binary_vars <- c("SMOKING", "YELLOW_FINGERS", "ANXIETY", "PEER_PRESSURE", "CHRONIC.DISEASE", "FATIGUE", "ALLERGY", "WHEEZING", "ALCOHOL.CONSUMING", "COUGHING","SHORTNESS.OF.BREATH", "SWALLOWING.DIFFICULTY", "CHEST.PAIN")

lung_cancer[binary_vars] <- lapply(lung_cancer[binary_vars], function(x) ifelse(x == 2, 1, 0))

# Convert GENDER M/F to binary (M=1, F=0)
lung_cancer$GENDER <- ifelse(lung_cancer$GENDER == "M", 1, 0)

# Convert LUNG_CANCER Y/N into binary (YES=1,  NO=0)
lung_cancer$LUNG_CANCER <- ifelse(lung_cancer$LUNG_CANCER == "YES", 1, 0)

# Check for missing values

Features Analysis: Age Distribution on Balanced Data

# Create age groups matching 5-year bins
# Widen lower bound to avoid NA bin from any outlier ages
lung_cancer_balanced <- lung_cancer_balanced %>%
  mutate(AGE_GROUP = cut(AGE,
                          breaks = c(-Inf, 39, 44, 49, 54, 59, 64, 69, 74, 79, 84, Inf),
                          labels = c("35 -- 39", "40 -- 44", "45 -- 49", "50 -- 54",
                                     "55 -- 59", "60 -- 64", "65 -- 69", "70 -- 74",
                                     "75 -- 79", "80 -- 84", "85+"),
                          right = TRUE))

# Confirm no NAs remain
sum(is.na(lung_cancer_balanced$AGE_GROUP))
[1] 0
# Calculate percentage as share of the WHOLE balanced dataset (not within-group)
age_group_pct <- lung_cancer_balanced %>%
  count(LUNG_CANCER, AGE_GROUP, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) %>%   # denominator = total rows in balanced data
  mutate(LUNG_CANCER = factor(LUNG_CANCER, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")))

# Plot: grouped bar chart with percentages (matches paper's Figure 1)
ggplot(age_group_pct, aes(x = AGE_GROUP, y = pct, fill = LUNG_CANCER)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.01),
                      limits = c(0, 0.2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#4472C4", "Yes" = "#ED7D31")) +
  labs(title = "Lung Cancer",

3.3 Features Analysis: Feature Ranking (Table 1)

# Random Forest Feature Importance (Gini-based)

ranking_data <- lung_cancer_balanced %>%
  select(!AGE_GROUP)

set.seed(123)

rf_model <- randomForest(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = ranking_data,
  importance = TRUE,
  ntree = 500
)

rf_importance <- importance(rf_model, type = 2) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Feature") %>%
  rename(RF_Ranking = MeanDecreaseGini) %>%
  arrange(desc(RF_Ranking))

rf_importance
# Gain Ratio
# Formula: GR(fi) = [H(c) - H(c|fi)] / H(fi)

# Entropy function: H(X) = -sum(p * log2(p))
entropy <- function(x) {
  probs <- table(x) / length(x)
  probs <- probs[probs > 0]  # avoid log(0)
  -sum(probs * log2(probs))
}

# Conditional entropy function: H(c|f) = sum over f's values of P(f=v) * H(c | f=v)
conditional_entropy <- function(class_var, feature_var) {
  levels_f <- unique(feature_var)
  total_n <- length(feature_var)
  
  cond_h <- 0
  for (v in levels_f) {
    subset_class <- class_var[feature_var == v]
    weight <- length(subset_class) / total_n
    cond_h <- cond_h + weight * entropy(subset_class)
  }
  return(cond_h)
}# Gain Ratio function for one feature
gain_ratio_single <- function(class_var, feature_var) {
  h_c <- entropy(class_var)
  h_c_given_f <- conditional_entropy(class_var, feature_var)
  h_f <- entropy(feature_var)
  
  info_gain <- h_c - h_c_given_f
  
  # Avoid divide-by-zero if feature has only 1 unique value
  if (h_f == 0) return(0)
  
  gr <- info_gain / h_f
  return(gr)
}
# Apply Gain Ratio to all features

feature_names <- setdiff(names(ranking_data), "LUNG_CANCER")
class_var <- ranking_data$LUNG_CANCER

gr_scores <- sapply(feature_names, function(f) {
  gain_ratio_single(class_var, ranking_data[[f]])
})

gain_ratio_result <- data.frame(
  Feature = names(gr_scores),
  GR_Ranking = round(as.numeric(gr_scores), 4)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(GR_Ranking))

gain_ratio_result
# Combine into Table 1 format (Random Forest | Gain Ratio side by side)

table1 <- data.frame(
  RF_Feature = rf_importance$Feature,
  RF_Ranking = round(rf_importance$RF_Ranking, 4),
  GR_Feature = gain_ratio_result$Feature,
  GR_Ranking = gain_ratio_result$GR_Ranking
)

kable_table <- kable(
  table1,
  caption = "<b>Feature Selection for Early Lung Cancer Detection</b>",
  col.names = c("Feature (RF)", "Score (RF)", "Feature (Gain Ratio)", "Score (Gain Ratio)"),
  align = c("l", "c", "l", "c")
)

print(kable_table)

# List of binary features to summarize (excludes AGE - it's continuous)
binary_features <- c("GENDER", "SMOKING", "YELLOW_FINGERS", "ANXIETY", 
                      "PEER_PRESSURE", "CHRONIC.DISEASE", "FATIGUE", "ALLERGY", 
                      "WHEEZING", "ALCOHOL.CONSUMING", "COUGHING", 
                      "SHORTNESS.OF.BREATH", "SWALLOWING.DIFFICULTY", "CHEST.PAIN")

# Force all binary feature columns to numeric before rounding
# (as.character first avoids the classic factor -> wrong-number bug)
lung_cancer_balanced_rounded <- lung_cancer_balanced %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(binary_features), 
                ~ round(as.numeric(as.character(.)))))

# Confirm it worked

# Function: for one feature, compute % of whole dataset in each 
# Feature-value x LUNG_CANCER combination
feature_table2 <- function(feature_name, data) {
  data %>%
    count(!!sym(feature_name), LUNG_CANCER, .drop = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
    mutate(LUNG_CANCER = factor(LUNG_CANCER, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>%
    select(!!sym(feature_name), LUNG_CANCER, pct) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = LUNG_CANCER, values_from = pct) %>%
    rename(Value = !!sym(feature_name)) %>%
    mutate(Feature = feature_name, .before = Value)
}

# Apply to every binary feature and combine into one long table
table2_long <- map_dfr(binary_features, ~ feature_table2(.x, lung_cancer_balanced_rounded))

table2_long
# ============================================================
# Format Value labels (0/1 -> No/Yes, or Female/Male for gender)
# ============================================================

table2_formatted <- table2_long %>%
  mutate(Value = case_when(
    Feature == "GENDER" & Value == 0 ~ "Female",
    Feature == "GENDER" & Value == 1 ~ "Male",
    Value == 0 ~ "No",
    Value == 1 ~ "Yes",
    TRUE ~ as.character(Value)
  )) %>%
  mutate(No = round(No, 2), Yes = round(Yes, 2))

table2_formatted

4.1 Experiments Setup: Data Split

lung_cancer_balanced <- lung_cancer_balanced %>%
  select(!AGE_GROUP)

set.seed(123)

split <- initial_validation_split(lung_cancer_balanced, prop=c(0.7, 0.1))

train_set <- training(split)
test_set <- testing(split)
validation_set <- validation(split)
# For submission
write.csv(train_set, "training.csv")
write.csv(test_set, "testing.csv")
write.csv(validation_set, "validation.csv")

4.1 Experiments Setup: Creating ML Models

Every model requires 10-fold cross validation. We are setting this up here:

# General
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(123)
cv_folds <- createFolds(train_set$LUNG_CANCER, k = 10, returnTrain = TRUE)

# Shared 10-Fold CV Control
train_ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  index = cv_folds,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

Naive Bayes

# 1. Fixed helper function to handle mdlp cut points (by column position/name)
apply_mdlp_cuts <- function(data, cutp) {
  discretized_data <- data
  
  for (i in seq_along(names(data))) {
    col <- names(data)[i]
    # mdlp() stores cut points in cutp[[i]]
    cuts <- cutp[[i]] 
    
    if (!is.null(cuts) && !all(is.na(cuts)) && cuts[1] != "All") {
      breaks <- c(-Inf, as.numeric(cuts), Inf)
      discretized_data[[col]] <- as.integer(
        cut(data[[col]], breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
      )
    } else {
      discretized_data[[col]] <- 1L
    }
  }
  return(discretized_data)
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Implement Supervised Discretization
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure target is a factor
train_set$LUNG_CANCER <- as.factor(train_set$LUNG_CANCER)
test_set$LUNG_CANCER  <- as.factor(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)

# Subset AGE and LUNG_CANCER for MDLP (MDLP requires target as the last column)
train_num <- train_set %>% select(AGE, LUNG_CANCER)

# Fit Fayyad & Irani's MDL model
mdlp_model <- mdlp(train_num)

# Extract discretized training feature
train_discretized <- mdlp_model$Disc.data

# Apply training cut points to test_set
test_discretized <- apply_mdlp_cuts(test_set[, "AGE", drop = FALSE], mdlp_model$cutp)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Reform Datasets
# -------------------------------------------------------------
numeric_cols <- "AGE"
cat_cols     <- c("GENDER", "SMOKING", "YELLOW_FINGERS", "ANXIETY", "PEER_PRESSURE", 
                  "CHRONIC.DISEASE", "FATIGUE", "ALLERGY", "WHEEZING", "ALCOHOL.CONSUMING", 
                  "COUGHING", "SHORTNESS.OF.BREATH", "SWALLOWING.DIFFICULTY", "CHEST.PAIN")

# Combine discretized AGE with categorical predictors and target
train_set_nb <- cbind(
  AGE = train_discretized[, "AGE"], 
  train_set[, cat_cols, drop = FALSE], 
  LUNG_CANCER = train_set$LUNG_CANCER
)

test_set_nb <- cbind(
  AGE = test_discretized[, "AGE"], 
  test_set[, cat_cols, drop = FALSE], 
  LUNG_CANCER = test_set$LUNG_CANCER
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Fit Naive Bayes (useKernelEstimator: False)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
tune_grid <- expand.grid(
  usekernel = FALSE, # Gaussian distribution assumption
  laplace = 0,
  adjust = 1
)

nb_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_set_nb,
  method = "naive_bayes",
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  tuneGrid = tune_grid
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Predict & Evaluate (Fixed variable name to test_set_nb)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
nb_preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_set_nb)

conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(nb_preds, test_set_nb$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix)

Bayesian Network (BayesNet)

# Ensure factors for bnlearn
train_bn <- data.frame(lapply(train_set_nb, as.factor))
test_bn  <- data.frame(lapply(test_set_nb, as.factor))

# Run 10-fold CV using the exact same fold indices
bn_cv_acc <- numeric(10)

for (i in 1:10) {
  train_idx <- cv_folds[[i]]
  fold_train <- train_bn[train_idx, ]
  fold_val   <- train_bn[-train_idx, ]
  
  # Learn structure (K2/Hill-Climbing) and parameters
  dag <- hc(fold_train)
  fitted <- bn.fit(dag, data = fold_train)
  
  preds <- predict(fitted, node = "LUNG_CANCER", data = fold_val)
  bn_cv_acc[i] <- mean(preds == fold_val$LUNG_CANCER)
}

cat("BayesNet 10-Fold CV Mean Accuracy:", mean(bn_cv_acc), "\n")
BayesNet 10-Fold CV Mean Accuracy: 0.7592333

Logistic Model Tree (LMT)

A Model-Based Recursive Partitioning Tree with Linear Regression is the alternative to Weka’s LMT.

library(partykit)
# --- Define formula ---
# Dependent variable ~ Split variables | Node logistic regression variables
lmt_formula <- LUNG_CANCER ~ . | .

# 1. Fit Final LMT Model on Full Training Set
lmt_model <- glmtree(
  lmt_formula,
  data = train_set,
  family = binomial,
  minsize = 15
)

# 2. Run Explicit 10-Fold Cross-Validation for LMT Metrics
set.seed(123)
cv_folds <- caret::createFolds(train_set$LUNG_CANCER, k = 10)
cv_accuracies <- numeric(10)

for (i in 1:10) {
  cv_train <- train_set[-cv_folds[[i]], ]
  cv_val   <- train_set[cv_folds[[i]], ]
  
  fold_fit <- glmtree(
    lmt_formula,
    data = cv_train,
    family = binomial,
    minsize = 15
  )
  
  # Predict probabilities and convert to hard class predictions
  fold_probs <- predict(fold_fit, newdata = cv_val, type = "response")
  fold_preds <- factor(
    ifelse(fold_probs > 0.5, levels(train_set$LUNG_CANCER)[2], levels(train_set$LUNG_CANCER)[1]),
    levels = levels(train_set$LUNG_CANCER)
  )
  
  cv_accuracies[i] <- mean(fold_preds == cv_val$LUNG_CANCER)
}

Rotation Forest (RotF)

library(caret)
library(dplyr)

fit_custom_rotation_forest <- function(train_df, test_df, target_col, L = 50, K = 3) {
  # 1. One-hot encode for PCA feature rotations
  formula_full <- as.formula(paste(target_col, "~ ."))
  dummy_proc   <- dummyVars(formula_full, data = train_df, fullRank = TRUE)
  
  X_train_mat <- predict(dummy_proc, newdata = train_df)
  X_test_mat  <- predict(dummy_proc, newdata = test_df)
  
  y_train <- train_df[[target_col]]
  pos_class <- levels(y_train)[2]
  
  n_samples <- nrow(X_train_mat)
  n_features <- ncol(X_train_mat)
  
  test_prob_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(X_test_mat), ncol = L)
  
  for (i in 1:L) {
    # Bootstrap sample
    boot_idx <- sample(1:n_samples, replace = TRUE)
    X_boot   <- X_train_mat[boot_idx, ]
    
    # Feature group partitioning
    feat_indices <- sample(1:n_features)
    groups       <- split(feat_indices, ceiling(seq_along(feat_indices) / K))
    
    # Build transformation rotation matrix R
    R_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_features, ncol = n_features)
    
    for (grp in groups) {
      if (length(grp) == 0) next
      sub_data <- X_boot[, grp, drop = FALSE]
      
      # Perform PCA on feature subset
      pca_res <- prcomp(sub_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
      
      # Fill rotation loadings
      for (col_i in seq_along(grp)) {
        R_matrix[grp, grp[col_i]] <- pca_res$rotation[, col_i]
      }
    }
    
    # Rotate data into PC space
    X_train_rot <- as.data.frame(X_train_mat %*% R_matrix)
    X_test_rot  <- as.data.frame(X_test_mat %*% R_matrix)
    
    X_train_rot[[target_col]] <- y_train
    
    # Train base decision tree on rotated space
    tree_fit <- train(
      formula_full,
      data = X_train_rot,
      method = "rpart",
      trControl = trainControl(method = "none"),
      tuneGrid = expand.grid(cp = 0.01)
    )
    
    # Predict probabilities for this rotated tree
    preds_prob <- predict(tree_fit, newdata = X_test_rot, type = "prob")[, pos_class]
    test_prob_matrix[, i] <- preds_prob
  }
  
  # Average predictions across all L rotated trees
  rowMeans(test_prob_matrix)
}

# --- Run Rotation Forest & Extract Probabilities ---
positive_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[2]
prob_rotf      <- fit_custom_rotation_forest(train_set, test_set, "LUNG_CANCER", L = 50, K = 3)

# Check probabilities vector
head(prob_rotf)

library(adabag)

  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,

  boos = FALSE,

)

# 2. Predict on test set
adaboost_pred_obj <- predict.boosting(adaboost_model, newdata = test_set)

# 3. Extract positive class probabilities safely by column index
pos_class_index <- which(levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER) == positive_class)
prob_adaboost   <- adaboost_pred_obj$prob[, pos_class_index]

# 4. Generate hard class predictions & confusion matrix
adaboost_preds <- factor(adaboost_pred_obj$class, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
conf_matrix_adaboost <- confusionMatrix(adaboost_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_adaboost)

# 1. Train MLP Model
mlp_model <- train(
  LUNG_CANCER ~ .,
  data = train_set,
  method = "nnet",
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(
    size = c(3, 5),       # Hidden units
    decay = c(0.01, 0.1)  # Regularization parameter
  ),
  trControl = train_ctrl,
  trace = FALSE
)

# 2. Discrete Class Predictions & Confusion Matrix
mlp_preds <- predict(mlp_model, newdata = test_set)
conf_matrix_mlp <- confusionMatrix(mlp_preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
print(conf_matrix_mlp)

# 1. Define positive class label (e.g., "YES")
positive_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[2]

# 2. Extract predicted probabilities for the positive class
prob_nb  <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_set_nb, type = "prob")[, positive_class]

# BayesNet (bnlearn)
prob_bn_raw <- predict(bn_final, node = "LUNG_CANCER", data = test_bn, prob = TRUE)
prob_bn     <- attr(prob_bn_raw, "prob")[positive_class, ]

prob_sgd <- predict(sgd_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_svm <- predict(svm_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_lr  <- predict(lr_model,  newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_ann <- predict(ann_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_knn <- predict(knn_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_dt  <- predict(dt_model,  newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_lmt <- predict(lmt_model, newdata = test_set, type = "response")
prob_rf <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_rt <- predict(rt_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]
prob_mlp <- predict(mlp_model, newdata = test_set, type = "prob")[, positive_class]

# 3. Calculate pROC objects
roc_nb  <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_nb,  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_bn  <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_bn,  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_sgd <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_sgd, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_svm <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_svm, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_lr  <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_lr,  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_ann <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_ann, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_knn <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_knn, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_dt  <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_dt,  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_lmt <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_lmt, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_rf <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rf, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_rt <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rt, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_rotf <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_rotf, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_adaboost <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_adaboost, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))
roc_mlp <- roc(test_set$LUNG_CANCER, prob_mlp, levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER))

# 4. Plot Overlaying ROC Curves
plot(roc_nb,  col = "red",         main = "ROC Curves Comparison across Models", legacy.axes = TRUE)
plot(roc_bn,  col = "blue",        add = TRUE)
plot(roc_sgd, col = "green",       add = TRUE)
plot(roc_svm, col = "purple",      add = TRUE)

library(knitr)

# Define positive class label (e.g., "YES" or "1")
positive_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[2]

neg_class <- levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)[1]

rotf_preds <- factor(
  ifelse(prob_rotf > 0.5, positive_class, neg_class),
  levels = levels(test_set$LUNG_CANCER)
)

# --- Helper Function to Extract Metrics safely from Confusion Matrix ---
get_metrics <- function(predictions, actual, pos_class) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(predictions, actual, positive = pos_class)
  
  acc <- cm$overall["Accuracy"]
  prec <- cm$byClass["Precision"]
  rec  <- cm$byClass["Sensitivity"] # Sensitivity = Recall
  
  return(c(Accuracy = unname(acc), Precision = unname(prec), Recall = unname(rec)))
}

# --- Compile Predictions from All Models ---
# Assumes each model's predicted class factor vector is stored from earlier steps:
models_preds <- list(
  "Naive Bayes"         = nb_preds,
  "BayesNet"            = bn_preds,
  "SGD"                 = sgd_preds,
  "Linear SVM"          = svm_preds,
  "Logistic Regression" = glm_preds,
  "ANN"                 = ann_preds,
  "KNN (K=3)"           = knn_preds,
  "C5.0 Tree"           = c50_preds,
  "Random Forest"       = rf_preds,
  "Random Tree"         = rt_preds,
  "REPTree"             = reptree_preds,
  "LMT (glmtree)"       = lmt_preds,
  "Rotation Forest"     = rotf_preds,
  "AdaBoost.M1"         = adaboost_preds,
  "ML Perceptron"       = mlp_preds
)

# Build metrics matrix
results_list <- lapply(models_preds, function(preds) {
  get_metrics(preds, test_set$LUNG_CANCER, pos_class = positive_class)
})

# Convert list to Data Frame
benchmark_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Model") %>%
  mutate(
    Accuracy  = round(Accuracy, 4),
    Precision = round(Precision, 4),
    Recall    = round(Recall, 4)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Accuracy)) # Sort by highest accuracy

# Render formatted HTML/Markdown table
kable_table <- kable(
  benchmark_df,
  caption = "<b>Performance Summary across Machine Learning Models</b>",
  col.names = c("Model", "Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall"),
  align = c("l", "c", "c", "c")
)

# Print the table
